summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease, and orthostatic hypotension was admitted for chest pressure similar to prior myocardial infarction. The episode occurred in the setting of dehydration and significant orthostatic blood pressure drop. Initial EKG showed transient ST depressions, but troponins remained negative and repeat EKG was normal. The chest pain resolved with 5 liters of IV fluids. Abdominal pain in the right lower quadrant, likely due to gas or diverticulosis, also resolved without intervention. The patient was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to increase oral fluid and salt intake, use compression stockings, and follow up with cardiology and autonomics. No changes were made to his baseline medications except for switching aspirin to a lower dose for safety.
